tools.name: add_cases_to_collection
tools.description: Add test cases to an existing test collection. Cases must exist and belong to the same project. Duplicate cases are skipped.

caseIds.description: Numeric test case IDs to add (e.g., [1, 2, 3])

tools.name: add_cases_to_execution
tools.description: Add individual test cases to a Manual Test Execution as a new named group. Unlike suites and Collections, loose cases have no identity of their own, so name is required and the group it creates is what appears in the execution; the call returns its groupId. caseIds are NUMERIC ids, never TC-numbers. Use add_suites_to_execution or add_collections_to_execution when the cases are already gathered into one of those. Cases from another project are skipped, and an empty result creates no group. Returns {added, skipped, groupId}.

tools.name: add_collections_to_execution
tools.description: Add whole Test Collections to a Manual Test Execution. Each is snapshotted in and keeps its own identity inside the execution. Pick this when the work is already gathered into a Collection. Use add_suites_to_execution to take the current cases of a suite instead, and add_cases_to_execution for loose cases, which need a new named group. Collections from another project are skipped, as are shadow collections, and one already in the execution is skipped rather than snapshotted twice. Returns {added, skipped}.

tools.name: add_external_link
tools.description: Link any test entity (case/execution/release/launch) to an external ticket in Jira, Linear, GitHub, GitLab, or any other system. Returns the link record: id (the link UUID that remove_external_link takes), provider, externalId, externalUrl, externalTitle, externalStatus, linkType, providerMetadata, createdAt. Idempotent: the same provider plus externalId on the same entity refreshes the stored URL and title and returns that link instead of adding a duplicate. Provider jira has a side effect: title and canonical URL are read from the Jira API, and when the organization has remote links enabled a Remote Link is pushed back onto the Jira issue, so a failure there comes back as remoteLinkWarning while the local link still stands. Call list_external_links to see what an entity is already linked to and to get link ids, and remove_external_link to delete one by its link UUID.

entityType.description: Type of M00N entity to link.

entityId.description: Entity ID: numeric integer for case, UUID string for the others.

externalId.description: External ticket key/number, e.g. PROJ-123, ENG-456, #42. For Jira, also accepts a full issue URL (e.g. https://yourorg.atlassian.net/browse/PROJ-123) - the key is extracted automatically.

externalUrl.description: Full URL to the external ticket. Required for non-Jira providers. Optional for Jira (the canonical URL is fetched from the Jira API).

externalTitle.description: Optional title/summary of the ticket. Ignored for Jira (title comes from the Jira API).

tools.name: add_suites_to_execution
tools.description: Add whole Suites to a Manual Test Execution. The cases each suite holds are snapshotted in as they stand now, and the suite keeps its own identity inside the execution. Pick this when the work is organised by suite. Use add_collections_to_execution when it is already gathered into a Test Collection, and add_cases_to_execution for loose cases, which need a new named group instead. Suites from another project are skipped, and a suite already in the execution is skipped rather than snapshotted twice. Returns {added, skipped}.

tools.name: bulk_update_cases
tools.description: Update multiple test cases at once. Supports updating status, priority, and tags for a batch of cases. All cases must belong to the same project.

caseIds.description: Array of numeric case IDs to update (e.g., [1, 2, 3])

addTags.description: Tags to add to all cases

removeTags.description: Tags to remove from all cases

updates.description: Updates to apply. At least one field must be provided.

tools.name: create_execution
tools.description: Create a Manual Test Execution, the top-level container on the Executions page, which aggregates Test Collections, suites and named case groups. NOT the same as a Test Collection: use create_test_collection for a single grouping of cases, and this to assemble an execution out of several. Returns the whole execution under an execution key: id, name, description, status, priority, environment, assignedTo, startDate, endDate, projectId and createdAt. The id you need for everything else is execution.id, not a top-level id. It starts empty, so follow with add_suites_to_execution, add_collections_to_execution or add_cases_to_execution to put something in it.

status.description: Optional. One of: not_executed, in_testing, passed, failed, blocked (plus any project-custom values). Defaults to 'not_executed'.

priority.description: Optional. One of: low, medium, high, critical. Defaults to 'medium'.

assignedTo.description: Optional assignee user id (must be a project member)

tools.name: create_folder
tools.description: Create a folder or a suite in a project. Use type "suite" for a leaf that holds test cases, and "folder" for a container that holds other folders and suites. Omitting type gives "folder" at the root and "suite" when nested, which is usually what you want. Suites cannot be parents, so a suite always needs parentId. Returns the new folder id, its type, and its path. To read an existing one use get_folder; to list them use list_folders.

projectId.description: Project UUID to create folder in

parentId.description: Parent folder UUID. Omit for root-level folder. Note: suites cannot be parents.

type.description: OPTIONAL - auto-detected. "folder" can contain children, "suite" is a leaf for test cases. Defaults to "folder" at root, "suite" when nested.

tools.name: create_release
tools.description: Create a new release in a project. Releases track versions and aggregate manual and automated test results. projectId comes from list_projects. Omit status to default to "planned". Returns the created release with id, name, version, description, status, startDate, endDate, projectId, projectName, createdAt and updatedAt; keep the id, it is what the other release tools take. Not idempotent - calling twice with the same name creates two separate releases, so check list_releases first. When the release already exists and only its name, version, dates or status should change, use update_release instead. The new release starts empty and nothing else is modified: attach automated launches with link_launches_to_release, and attach manual executions from the execution side via the releaseIds argument of create_execution or update_execution.

projectId.description: Project UUID to create release in

description.description: Detailed description of the release scope

status.description: OPTIONAL - defaults to "planned". Valid: planned, in_progress, completed, cancelled.

tools.name: create_test_case
tools.description: Create a new test case in a test suite. Test cases MUST live inside a suite (not a bare folder). You can provide either: (A) a folderId pointing to an existing suite, or (B) a projectId with optional folderName/suiteName to auto-create the folder→suite hierarchy. If folderId points to a folder (not a suite), a suite is auto-created inside it. Returns the full created case object including shareUrl. Tags are auto-created if they do not exist. IMPORTANT: Omit status and priority to use sensible defaults (Draft, Medium).

folderId.description: Suite (or folder) UUID where the case will be created. If this points to a folder, a suite is auto-created inside it. Alternative: use projectId + folderName + suiteName instead.

projectId.description: Project UUID. Required when folderId is not provided. Used to find or auto-create the folder→suite hierarchy.

folderName.description: Name of the folder to find or create (default: "General"). Used with projectId when folderId is not provided.

suiteName.description: Name of the suite to find or create inside the folder (default: "General"). Used with projectId when folderId is not provided.

description.description: Detailed description of the test case. Supports Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, inline `code`, # / ## / ### headings, "- " bullet and "1. " numbered lists, [text](url) links, and "> " blockquotes. Plain text works too. Images and fenced code blocks are not supported.

action.description: Step action to perform. Supports Markdown (**bold**, *italic*, `code`, lists, [links](url)). Plain text is fine.

expected.description: Expected result. Supports Markdown (**bold**, *italic*, `code`, lists, [links](url)). Plain text is fine.

steps.description: Array of test steps with action and expected result

status.description: OPTIONAL - defaults to "Draft". Only specify if user explicitly requests a different status. Valid values vary by project (typically: Draft, Ready, Approved, Deprecated).

priority.description: OPTIONAL - defaults to "Medium". Only specify if user explicitly requests a different priority. Valid values vary by project (typically: Low, Medium, High, Critical).

tags.description: Tags to assign to the case. New tags are auto-created.

dependsOn.description: Numeric case ID this case depends on

customFields.description: Custom field values as key-value pairs

externalLinks.description: Optional list of external ticket links to attach to the created case. Each link is inserted atomically with the case - any failure rolls back the entire creation. For Jira, externalUrl is fetched from the Jira API (just pass the issue key or full /browse/ URL as externalId); for other providers, externalUrl is required.

externalId.description: External ticket key/number. For Jira, also accepts a full /browse/ URL.

externalUrl.description: Full URL to the external ticket. Required for non-Jira providers; optional for Jira.

tools.name: create_test_collection
tools.description: Create a Test Collection and optionally add test cases to it. This is one Test Collection, NOT the top-level Executions-page container - use create_execution for that (an execution can then include this collection via add_collections_to_execution). Returns the created collection with count of added tests. Omit priority to default to "medium".

projectId.description: Project UUID to create collection in

description.description: Detailed description of the test collection

folderId.description: Folder UUID to place collection in (omit for root level)

priority.description: OPTIONAL - defaults to "medium". Valid: low, medium, high, critical.

assignedTo.description: Email address of the assigned tester

caseIds.description: Numeric test case IDs to add to collection (e.g., [1, 2, 3])

tools.name: delete_execution
tools.description: Soft-delete an entire Manual Test Execution (and unlink any Test Collections that pointed to it). Reversible only via support/DB - use with care. To remove just one source group instead, use remove_source_from_execution. Returns { deleted: true }.

tools.name: delete_folder
tools.description: Soft delete (archive) a folder and all its contents. Archives all nested folders and test cases recursively. Can be restored via the UI.

tools.name: delete_release
tools.description: Soft delete (archive) a release. The release can be restored via the UI. All linked Test Collections and launches are preserved.

tools.name: delete_test_case
tools.description: Soft delete (archive) a test case. The case can be restored via the UI. Also unlinks any connected autotests.

caseId.description: Numeric test case ID to archive

tools.name: delete_test_collection
tools.description: Archive (soft delete) a test collection. The collection can be restored via the UI. Test executions are preserved.

tools.name: export_report
tools.description: Generate a formatted report for a project. Supports summary, failures, trends, and release reports in markdown or JSON. Returns the report content as a string. NOTE: reportType "release" requires the releaseId argument (get it from list_releases).

projectId.description: Project UUID to generate report for

reportType.description: Type of report: summary (overview), failures (failed tests), trends (pass rate over time), release (release status)

releaseId.description: Release UUID (required for release report type)

tools.name: get_case_execution_history
tools.description: Get how one manual test case has fared over time, across every Manual Test Execution and release it appeared in, newest first. Returns the executions it was part of with the status recorded each time, plus totalExecutions and passRate. totalExecutions counts memberships, including times the case was added and never run, while passRate is computed over the rows actually executed, so the two do not divide into each other. IMPORTANT: days defaults to 30, so a case last tested longer ago returns almost nothing and reads as never tested; pass days explicitly for the full history. This covers MANUAL results only: use get_test_history for an automated test across launches, and get_execution_cases for the rows inside one execution.

caseId.description: Internal numeric test case id (the "id" from list_test_cases / get_test_case / create_test_case). This is NOT the user-facing "TC-N" number (caseNumber/displayId) - if the user gave you a "TC-N", resolve it first via list_test_cases(search: "TC-N") and use the returned id. Project is derived from the case.

limit.description: Maximum number of executions to return

tools.name: get_coverage_gaps
tools.description: Identify test coverage gaps across a whole project. Returns summary (totalCases, linkedCases, unlinkedCases, automationRate), foldersWithLowCoverage (folderId, name, caseCount, linkedCount, automationRate) for folders under automationThreshold, unlinkedCases (caseId, displayId, title, status, priority, folderName) for cases with no linked autotest, and the reverse gap unlinkedAutotests - autotests seen in the most recent launches that are linked to no case. Read-only, nothing is written; close a gap afterwards with link_autotest_to_case. Pick this when the question is which cases or folders lack automation project-wide. Prefer get_feature_scan when the scope is a single Jira issue and Jira is connected, run_health_check when you want one scored assessment in which coverage is only one dimension, search_tests when you already know the autotest and want its status, and suggest_test_cases when the gap is a case that does not exist yet rather than a missing link. projectId comes from list_projects.

automationThreshold.description: Folders below this automation % are flagged as low coverage (default: 50)

includeUnlinkedCases.description: Include list of test cases without linked autotests

limit.description: Maximum number of unlinked cases to return

recentLaunches.description: How many of the most recent launches to scan for autotests that are not linked to any test case (reverse coverage gap). Default and max: 10.

tools.name: get_execution
tools.description: Get one Manual Test Execution with everything attached to it. Returns execution (the container itself), sources (one entry per suite, Collection or case group added, each with id, name, sourceType, status and the case counts total, passed, failed, blocked, inTesting and notExecuted), releases, externalLinks, and progress. sourceType is what tells a suite source from a Collection source. progress carries the same counts across the whole execution PLUS passRate and completionRate; the entries in sources do not carry those two, so compute them per source if you need them. Use get_execution_cases for the individual case rows, which is also where report_case_result gets its executionCaseId; use list_executions to find an id.

tools.name: get_execution_cases
tools.description: List the individual case-run rows of a Manual Test Execution so you can report results against them. Returns each row's executionCaseId (UUID - pass to report_case_result), caseId (numeric), group, current status, the case-level result fields (notes, causedBy, durationMinutes, executedBy, executedAt), the case's externalLinks (Jira/Linear tickets, present only if you also hold integrations:read), and steps (0-based index, action, expected, current step status, issueDescription). Everything report_case_result writes reads back here. Use after add_*_to_execution and before report_case_result. Supports paging + filtering by group/status/title.

groupId.description: Optional: only cases in this source group (execution_test_run UUID)

status.description: Optional case-status filter (e.g. not_executed, passed, failed)

tools.name: get_feature_scan
tools.description: Get a comprehensive feature health scan by Jira issue key. Returns Jira context (summary, status, type, assignee), test coverage stats (case count, automation ratio, pass rate, risk score), linked test cases, and autotest results with recent run trends. Automatically detects issue hierarchy and aggregates child issues (2 levels deep: epic→story→subtask). Requires Jira to be connected to the organization.

jiraKey.description: Jira issue key (e.g., PROJ-111). Can be any issue type - epics, stories, tasks, bugs, sub-tasks. Epics automatically aggregate all child issue data.

tools.name: get_folder
tools.description: Get one folder or suite by id. Returns id, name, type, parentId, projectId, projectName, path, depth, casesCount, childFolderCount, displayOrder, createdAt and updatedAt. casesCount counts cases DIRECTLY in this folder, so a container folder reports 0 however much sits beneath it; childFolderCount tells you whether that is the case. Set includeStats for a statistics object over the folder AND everything nested under it, which is where totalCases, automatedCases, automationRate, status and priority breakdowns, tag usage and time-based metrics live: expect statistics.totalCases to exceed casesCount. Set includeCases for the most recent cases directly in it, capped by casesLimit. Use list_folders to see the tree or find an id; use this when you have one id and want detail.

folderId.description: Folder UUID to get. Obtain from list_folders.

includeStats.description: Include detailed statistics (automation rate, status/priority breakdown)

includeCases.description: Include list of recent test cases in folder

casesLimit.description: Maximum number of cases to include (when includeCases=true)

tools.name: get_launch_tests
tools.description: Get every test inside one launch, with results, error messages and stack traces for the failures. Use this once you have a launch id, which get_launches_statistics gives you; use get_test_history to follow one test across launches instead. For each failed test that has artifacts the response carries an `attachments` array of `{ id, name, contentType, size, url }`. The `url` is fully qualified: if it is an API URL, fetch it with the same `X-MCP-Key` header you use for this server, while presigned storage URLs need no header. That is how you reach screenshots, traces, videos and source files when investigating a failure.

launchId.description: Run/launch UUID to get tests from. Obtain from get_launches_statistics or get_launches_trends.

statuses.description: Filter by test status (default: all statuses)

search.description: Search in test title path or file path

includeErrors.description: Include error details for failed tests

tools.name: get_launches_statistics
tools.description: List the launches of a project, newest first, each with its own pass, fail, skip and duration figures. Returns launches, a summary over the whole window (totalRuns, passedRuns, failedRuns, runningRuns, runPassRate, totalTests, totalPassed, totalFailed, totalSkipped, testPassRate, avgDurationSeconds), the period and filters applied, and pagination with the real total; there is no top-level total. IMPORTANT: days defaults to 30, so a project idle for longer returns an empty list, which means nothing in the window rather than nothing at all. Use limit, offset and search to page, statuses or tags to narrow. Reach for get_launches_trends when the question is about the project over time rather than about particular launches, and get_launch_tests when you have one launch and want the tests in it.

tools.name: get_launches_trends
tools.description: Aggregate a project over a window: pass rate over time, the tests that fail most, the flaky ones, duration trends and the slowest tests. IMPORTANT: the pass rate here is the share of LAUNCHES that ended green, not the share of tests that passed, and the two differ widely; for the test-level figure use summary.testPassRate from get_launches_statistics. Flakiness is ranked by flip_count, the number of times a test changed result between consecutive launches, alongside instability_score which weighs how evenly it splits between pass and fail. days defaults to 30, so a quiet project returns empty series. Use include[] to compute only the sections you need and topN to size the lists. Reach for get_launches_statistics to page through individual launches, and get_launch_tests when you have one launch.

topN.description: Limit for top-N lists (failing, flaky, slowest tests)

include.description: Which trends to include in response

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Get a project's configuration: its meta, the system-field vocabularies it actually uses (statuses/priorities/environments), and its case custom-field definitions. Call this to discover the VALID status values before setting them - e.g. execution_status (execution overall), test_case_execution_status (a case in an execution), test_run_status (a source group). Values are project-customizable, so do not hardcode them. Returns { project, systemFields{ case_status, case_priority, execution_status, test_case_execution_status, test_run_status, release_status, test_environment }, customFields[] }.

tools.name: get_release
tools.description: Get one release by releaseId with full detail: name, version, status, projectId, projectName, dates, and a stats rollup for linked manual executions (count, total, passed, failed, blocked, inTesting, notExecuted) and linked automated launches (count, total, passed, failed, skipped). By default it also returns the linkedExecutions and launches arrays, each entry with its own name, status, dates and per-item stats; set includeLinkedExecutions or includeLaunches to false to drop an array and keep the response small, since the stats rollup comes back either way. Use list_releases instead to browse, search or filter the releases in a project and to obtain releaseId; it returns the same rollup per release but never those two arrays, so call get_release once the release of interest is known. Read only, nothing is modified. An archived release still resolves here, unlike list_releases which hides it unless includeDeleted is set; the deleted flag in the response says which it is.

includeLinkedExecutions.description: Include the linked manual executions with per-execution stats. Set false to keep the response small - the stats.linkedExecutions totals are returned either way.

includeLaunches.description: Include linked automated launches with stats

tools.name: get_test_case
tools.description: Get one manual test case in full: id, caseNumber, displayId, title, description, status, priority, tags, ordered steps, folderId/folderName, projectId/projectName, dependsOn, customFields, createdAt/updatedAt and a shareUrl for pasting into Slack or Jira. Optional flags add linkedAutotests (includeLinkedAutotests, default true), recentAutotestExecutions from CI runs (includeRecentExecutions) and an edit-history audit trail (includeHistory). Read-only; nothing is modified. caseId is the internal numeric id from list_test_cases / create_test_case, not a user-facing TC-N; the project is derived from the case. Choose list_test_cases instead to browse, filter or count many cases, or to turn a TC-N into an id - it returns summaries without steps, so use it to pick the case and this tool to read it. Choose get_case_execution_history instead for how the case has fared in Manual Test Executions over time (pass rate plus an execution timeline); includeRecentExecutions here reports automated CI results only. search_tests covers automated tests, which are separate records from manual cases.

caseId.description: Internal numeric test case id (the "id" from list_test_cases / get_test_case / create_test_case). This is NOT the user-facing "TC-N" number (caseNumber/displayId) - if the user gave you a "TC-N", resolve it first via list_test_cases(search: "TC-N") and use the returned id. Project is derived from the case.

includeHistory.description: Include edit history (audit log of changes)

includeRecentExecutions.description: Include recent autotest execution results from CI runs

tools.name: get_test_collection
tools.description: Get one Test Collection by UUID. Returns metadata (name, status, priority, environment, assignedTo, project, folder, release, dates), stats (totalTests, passed, failed, blocked, notExecuted, skipped, inTesting), and unless includeTestDetails is false a tests array of caseId, caseNumber, caseTitle, casePriority, status, executedBy, executedAt, notes. Read-only, changes nothing. collectionId comes from list_test_collections, which is the tool for finding or comparing collections across a project rather than inspecting one. For a Manual Test Execution (the Executions-page container) use get_execution and get_execution_cases instead - a different entity, and only the rows returned by get_execution_cases can be reported against with report_case_result.

collectionId.description: Test collection UUID. Obtain from list_test_collections.

includeTestDetails.description: Include list of test cases with execution status

tools.name: get_test_history
tools.description: Get the history of one AUTOMATED test across launches, newest first, with the result and duration each time, plus totalExecutions, passRate, flipCount and reliabilityStatus. IMPORTANT: limit bounds the summary as well as the list, so those four figures describe the returned page rather than the whole window, and days defaults to 30. Match a test by its title, which search_tests will find for you. This covers automated results only: use get_case_execution_history for how a MANUAL case has fared, and get_launch_tests for every test inside one launch rather than one test across many.

titlePath.description: ONE segment of the title path, normally the test name itself (e.g. "should validate credentials"). Matching is a case-insensitive substring of the stored title-path array, so a " > "-joined path matches nothing and returns an empty history rather than an error. search_tests and get_launch_tests return titlePath as an array - pick one segment out of it.

limit.description: Maximum number of executions to return

tools.name: link_autotest_to_case
tools.description: Link an automated test (by title) to a manual test case for coverage tracking. The autotest does not need to exist yet (pre-linking is allowed). When that test next reports a result, it links to this case automatically.

caseId.description: Numeric test case ID to link to

testTitle.description: The test title to link, e.g., "should validate credentials" or "[E-SO-16] should allow editing..."

tools.name: link_launches_to_release
tools.description: Link launches to a release. Unlike Test Collections, which are copied in, launches are linked by reference.

releaseId.description: Release UUID to link launches to

launchIds.description: Run/launch UUIDs to link to the release. Obtain from get_launches_statistics.

tools.name: list_executions
tools.description: List Manual Test Executions for a project with progress stats. Use to find an existing execution id before adding sources. progress carries every case bucket (passed/failed/blocked/inTesting/notExecuted, which sum to total) plus passRate and completionRate.

tools.name: list_external_links
tools.description: List external ticket links for a given entity, optionally filtered by provider.

entityId.description: Entity ID (numeric for case, UUID otherwise).

tools.name: list_folders
tools.description: List the folder and suite tree of a project as a flat array under folders, with a total count. Every row carries id, name, type (folder or suite), parentId, path, depth, casesCount (cases directly in it, so 0 for most containers), childFolderCount, displayOrder, createdAt and updatedAt, which is enough to rank folders by size or to find the suites without a second call. Use this to browse or to find an id, then get_folder for one folder in detail with optional statistics over its whole subtree. Suites are the leaf nodes that hold test cases; use list_test_cases for the cases themselves.

projectId.description: Project UUID to list folders from

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List all projects accessible to the current user. START HERE - call this first to get project IDs needed for other tools. Admins see all org projects; managers/users see only assigned projects.

tools.name: list_releases
tools.description: List releases for a project with aggregated stats for manual tests and automated launches. Supports filtering by status and search.

projectId.description: Project UUID to list releases from

search.description: Search in release name, version, or description

tools.name: list_test_cases
tools.description: List test cases in a project with filtering and pagination. Can filter by folder, status, priority, tags, or search query. Returns available status/priority values in metadata for filter options. Each case includes a shareUrl for sharing in Slack, Jira, etc. To resolve a user-facing "TC-30" (displayId) to its internal numeric id, pass search: "TC-30" - search matches the case number and accepts the "TC-" prefix - then read the matching case id.

projectId.description: Project UUID to list cases from

folderId.description: Filter by specific folder UUID. Omit to list all cases in project.

status.description: Filter by case status (e.g., Draft, Ready, Approved). Values are project-specific.

priority.description: Filter by priority (e.g., Low, Medium, High, Critical). Values are project-specific.

search.description: Search in case title, description, or case number

automationStatus.description: Filter by automation status: "automated" (has linked autotests) or "not_automated" (no linked autotests)

tools.name: list_test_collections
tools.description: List Test Collections in a project - the groupings used for sprint, release or ad-hoc manual testing. Each entry returns id, name, status, priority, environment, assignedTo, folderId/folderName, releaseId/releaseName, start and end dates, and stats (totalTests, passed, failed, blocked, notExecuted, skipped, inTesting), plus a pagination block. Use it to find a collection UUID, filtered by folder, release or status; then call get_test_collection for one collection with its individual test cases and their execution status. A Test Collection is one grouping of cases, not the top-level Executions-page container, so use list_executions to find those. For the case library itself rather than runs of it, use list_test_cases. Shadow collections created inside an execution are never listed, and archived ones only with includeDeleted.

projectId.description: Project UUID to list collections from

folderId.description: Filter by folder UUID. Omit to list all collections.

rootOnly.description: If true, only return collections not in any folder (root level)

tools.name: move_test_case
tools.description: Move a test case to a different folder within the same project. Cross-project moves are not supported.

caseId.description: Numeric test case ID to move

targetFolderId.description: Target folder UUID (must be in the same project)

tools.name: remove_cases_from_collection
tools.description: Remove test cases from a test collection. Returns collectionId, collectionName and removed (count of case rows actually deleted); ids not present in the collection are ignored rather than raising an error. Destructive and not reversible: the recorded status and step results for those cases in this collection are deleted with them, while the test cases themselves stay in the project library. add_cases_to_collection is the inverse. To retire the whole collection instead use delete_test_collection, which archives it and preserves executions; to drop a source group from an Executions-page container use remove_source_from_execution; to archive the case itself project-wide use delete_test_case. collectionId comes from list_test_collections; caseIds are the numeric internal ids from list_test_cases, not TC-numbers.

caseIds.description: Numeric test case IDs to remove (e.g., [1, 2, 3])

tools.name: remove_external_link
tools.description: Remove an external ticket link by its link UUID (as returned by add_external_link or list_external_links).

tools.name: remove_source_from_execution
tools.description: Remove a source group (a suite, collection, or named case-group - one execution_test_run) from an execution. This deletes that group and ALL its case-run rows and step results (cascade). Get the runId (group id) from get_execution (sources[].id) or get_execution_cases (groupId). Does not delete the execution itself. Returns { removed: true }.

runId.description: Source group UUID (execution_test_run id) to remove

tools.name: report_case_result
tools.description: Record the result of running one case inside a Manual Test Execution: set per-step pass/fail and/or the case status, atomically and idempotently. Target the case by executionCaseId (from get_execution_cases) OR by executionId + caseId (numeric; if the case is in several groups, pass groupId or use executionCaseId). status: an explicit value (passed/failed/blocked/in_testing/not_executed), or "auto" to derive it from the steps (failed then blocked then in_testing then passed), or omit it to leave the case status unchanged (e.g. when only writing one step). steps[].status is one of not_executed/passed/failed/blocked/skipped; index is the 0-based position in the case steps. The containing source group's status auto-rolls from its cases' results: all not_executed -> not_started, some executed -> in_progress, all executed -> blocked if the group contains a blocked case, else completed (test_run_status has no failed; failures show via the group's counters). An explicit set_execution_source_status override lasts until the next report on that group recomputes it. Returns the case status, the group status, the steps written, and fresh execution progress.

executionCaseId.description: The case-run row UUID (from get_execution_cases). Preferred.

executionId.description: Alternative to executionCaseId: the execution UUID (with caseId).

caseId.description: Alternative to executionCaseId: the numeric case id (with executionId).

groupId.description: Optional: disambiguate when the case is in several source groups.

status.description: Case status: passed/failed/blocked/in_testing/not_executed, or "auto" to derive from steps, or omit to leave unchanged.

index.description: 0-based step index into the case steps

issueDescription.description: Optional note / issue / Jira link for a failed step

parentCaseId.description: Optional: set for a prerequisite (parent) case step

causedBy.description: Optional: which step or thing caused failure

notes.description: Optional free-text notes for the case run

tools.name: run_health_check
tools.description: Get a holistic health assessment for a project: a composite score from 0 to 100 blending automation stability, coverage and manual execution, plus per-dimension subScores and sections for automation (pass rate, flaky, failures), testAssets (case and suite counts, status and priority breakdown), coverage (automation rate and pass-rate trend), manualExecution (pass, fail, blocked, completion) and releases (status counts and active releases). IMPORTANT: days defaults to 14 here while get_launches_trends defaults to 30, so pass the same days to both before comparing their answers. Use include[] to limit which sections are computed. Reach for get_coverage_gaps when you want the specific cases and folders that lack automation rather than one score, and get_feature_scan when the scope is a single Jira issue.

include.description: Which sections to compute. Defaults to all. The composite score uses whichever of automation/coverage/manualExecution are present and have data.

tools.name: search_tests
tools.description: Search for tests by title, file path, or tags. Returns matching tests with their most recent execution status and reliability metrics. Use this to find tests related to a specific feature or area.

query.description: Search query (case-insensitive substring of the title-path array or the file path). Pass ONE title segment, e.g. "should validate credentials"; a " > "-joined path matches nothing.

limit.description: Maximum number of tests to return

tools.name: set_execution_source_status
tools.description: Set the status of one source group (a collection, suite, or named case-group - the per-group status dropdown on the execution page) inside an execution. Get the runId (group id) from get_execution (sources[].id) or get_execution_cases (groupId). status is validated against the project's test_run_status values (default: not_started, in_progress, completed, blocked) - call get_project to confirm. This is the GROUP status; use report_case_result for an individual case's status.

tools.name: suggest_test_cases
tools.description: Return template-based test case scaffolding for a feature description: structured ideas with titles, steps and priorities. This is pattern matching, not model output. Use it as a project-aware starting point, refine it yourself, then persist the result with create_test_case.

projectId.description: Project UUID for context (uses project settings for status/priority values)

featureDescription.description: Description of the feature to generate test cases for. Be specific about functionality, user flows, and edge cases.

testType.description: Type of test cases to suggest

maxSuggestions.description: Maximum number of test case suggestions

tools.name: unlink_launch_from_release
tools.description: Remove an automated launch from a release. The launch itself is not affected.

tools.name: update_execution
tools.description: Update a Manual Test Execution's own fields, including its overall status. Set status to in_testing while running, and passed/failed/blocked when done. status is validated against the project's execution_status values (default: not_executed, in_testing, passed, failed, blocked) - call get_project to read the exact values a project uses; do not hardcode. Does not change case results - use report_case_result for those, or set_execution_source_status for a source group's status.

status.description: Execution status: not_executed/in_testing/passed/failed/blocked (+ project-custom). Use get_project to confirm valid values.

assignedTo.description: Assignee user id (must be a project member)

releaseIds.description: Optional. The COMPLETE set of releases this execution should be linked to (replace-all): existing links not in the list are removed, new ones added. Pass [] to unlink all. Omit to leave links untouched. Release ids must belong to the execution's project.

tools.name: update_folder
tools.description: Rename a folder or suite and/or re-parent it. Set parentId to null to move it to root level, or omit it to keep the current parent. Returns the updated id, name, type, parentId, path, depth, casesCount and childFolderCount. A move carries everything nested inside along with it, so child paths change too; the new parent must be a folder in the same project, since suites cannot be parents and a folder cannot move into itself or into one of its own descendants. It never changes type and never creates or removes anything: use create_folder for a new folder or suite, delete_folder to archive one with all its contents, and move_test_case to relocate a single test case rather than its whole suite. Get folderId from list_folders.

parentId.description: New parent folder UUID. Set to null to move to root level. Omit to keep current parent.

tools.name: update_release
tools.description: Update release metadata. Only provided fields are updated; omitted fields remain unchanged. Use get_release first to see current values.

status.description: New status: planned, in_progress, completed, or cancelled. Setting to "completed" auto-sets completed_at timestamp.

tools.name: update_test_case
tools.description: Update an existing test case. Only provided fields are updated; omitted fields remain unchanged. Returns the full updated case object including shareUrl. TIP: Use get_test_case first to see current values.

caseId.description: Internal numeric test case id to update - NOT the user-facing "TC-N"/caseNumber. If the user gave you a "TC-N", resolve it via list_test_cases(search: "TC-N") first.

description.description: New description. Supports Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, inline `code`, # / ## / ### headings, "- " bullet and "1. " numbered lists, [text](url) links, and "> " blockquotes. Plain text works too. Images and fenced code blocks are not supported.

action.description: Step action. Supports Markdown (**bold**, *italic*, `code`, lists, [links](url)). Plain text is fine.

expected.description: Expected result. Supports Markdown (**bold**, *italic*, `code`, lists, [links](url)). Plain text is fine.

steps.description: Replace all steps with this array

status.description: New status. Typical values: Draft, Ready, Approved, Deprecated. Check list_test_cases meta.availableStatuses for project-specific values.

priority.description: New priority. Typical values: Low, Medium, High, Critical. Check list_test_cases meta.availablePriorities for project-specific values.

tags.description: Replace all tags with this array

dependsOn.description: Set dependency to another numeric case ID, or null to remove dependency

customFields.description: Custom field values (replaces all existing custom fields)

tools.name: update_test_collection
tools.description: Update test collection metadata. Only provided fields are updated; omitted fields remain unchanged. Use get_test_collection first to see current values.

status.description: New status: not_started, in_progress, completed, or blocked.

priority.description: New priority: low, medium, high, or critical.

assignedTo.description: Email address of the assigned tester (or empty to unassign)
